item.text:
Best read: **no**. I found only internal or Party-controlled oversight claims, not evidence that Xi strengthened independent institutions that could genuinely constrain him.

| Side | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Weak positive | The Party-state discipline system reported 47.7 million complaint-type reports in H1 2024 | CCDI / National Supervisory Commission | 2024-07-25 | https://www.ccdi.gov.cn/toutiaon/202407/t20240725_363777.html | Huge complaint intake and case-filing numbers suggest monitoring capacity, but it is Party discipline, not independent oversight. | 4B.4 |
| Weak positive | PRC public security authority complaint portal | Ministry of Public Security | 2024 | https://12389.mps.gov.cn/clue_reportNotice.action | The MPS runs a public complaint/reporting portal for police misconduct. This is a real channel, but it stays inside the security apparatus. | 4B.4, 3B.4 |
| Weak positive | Internal police inspectorate regulation | Local public security authority repost | 2024-02-01 | https://gaj.cq.gov.cn/zwgk/zfxxgkml/zcwj/xzfg/202402/t20240201_12890414.html | The regulation lets an internal inspectorate hear complaints and correct police decisions, but it is still inside the police chain of command. | 4B.4, 3B.4 |
| Negative | Xi’s discipline campaign was presented as strengthening discipline awareness and making cadres “loyal, clean and responsible” | Xinhua / english.www.gov.cn | 2024-05-26 | https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202405/26/content_WS66533ca6c6d0868f4e8e77c0.html | This shows internal discipline enforcement, not empowerment of bodies that can independently constrain Xi or the Party. | 4B.4, 3B.2 |
| Negative | The plenum reaffirmed national security and full Party self-governance | english.www.gov.cn / Xinhua | 2024-07-18 | https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202407/18/content_WS669906cdc6d0868f4e8e93db.html | Xi’s reform line emphasized centralized control and Party self-governance, not institutional independence. | 4B.4, 4B.2 |
| Negative | Hong Kong 47 democrats case | Reuters | 2024-05-30 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/hong-kongs-landmark-national-security-trial-for-47-democrats-3462427 | Mass pretrial detention, bail denial, and convictions show courts being used for political control, not as an independent check. | 4B.4, 4B.3, 4B.2 |
| Negative | Hong Kong’s new national security law broadens sabotage, sedition, and state-secrets offenses | Reuters | 2024-03-19 | https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/factboxscope-of-hong-kongs-new-national-security-laws-3344082 | Article 23 expanded the legal toolkit for control and reduced the space for courts to function as independent constraints. | 4B.4, 4B.2, 4B.3 |
| Negative | Hong Kong’s police complaints deficit | Human Rights Watch | 2024-06-10 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/06/10/hong-kong-no-accountability-5-years-after-mass-protests | HRW says there was no independent mechanism for police complaints, which is direct evidence against independent oversight. | 4B.4, 3B.4, 3B.9 |

**Synthesis**
- The positive material is mostly formal or internal: complaint hotlines, internal inspectorates, Party discipline statistics.
- None of that amounts to strengthening independent courts, legislatures, audit bodies, local governments, or oversight institutions that could constrain Xi.
- The clearer operational record is the opposite: centralized Party control, national security primacy, politicized Hong Kong courts, and no independent police accountability.

**Search gap**
- I found no credible 2024 evidence that Xi strengthened an institution precisely because it could constrain him.
- The closest positives are internal complaint mechanisms, but those are not independent and therefore do not satisfy the lens.
